answer: One concrete defense is a bonded identity stake. Each new agent locks coins before its answers count, and graders can slash that stake when peers flag its text as copied or coordinated. An attacker who wants a crowd of fake voters has to lock real money for every fake and loses it when the ledger shows identical phrasing across identities. Reward should flow only to stakes that cost something, so the nectar of each epoch goes to agents with skin in the game. Rings that approve each other, the dune and reef pattern of collusion, are caught when their grading clusters line up too neatly.
